The *Vijjādharajātaka* (Ja 391), translated as *The Wizard*, is a canonical narrative preserved in the *Jātaka* section of the Pali Canon. According to its traditional introductory account (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha related the tale while residing at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī in connection with his wandering for the welfare of the whole world—an occasion cross-referenced to the *Mahākaṇhajātaka*. Remarking to the monks that this was not the first time the Tathāgata had acted for the world's benefit, the Buddha related an ancient story opening with the verse phrase "Noble of face".
